conditions: Two coherent in-phase ideal narrow slits separated by positive d, far-field approximation in a uniform medium, monochromatic wavelength lambda>0, integer order m with |m lambda|<=d. Finite slit envelopes may suppress maxima.
spoken_aliases: d times sine of theta equals m times lambda
slit separation times sine of the observation angle equals interference order times wavelength

evidence: In the far-field approximation the signed geometric path-length difference in a uniform medium is d sin(theta). Coherent in-phase equal-frequency waves have constructive interference when this difference is an integer multiple of wavelength. This gives the bright-fringe condition for ideal narrow slits; finite slit diffraction can suppress orders.
